fact_check_verdict: Publish as a peer-reviewed research framework tested on one road transect. No accuracy figure is public, nothing says it is deployed. The risk percentages belong to a separate study of the Arctic Coastal Plain, and the dollar range to a 2025 study. Wainwright drone claim and 'can't be measured' wording were cut.

claims.spoken: A road in Utqiagvik sits on frozen ground.
Researchers buried two fiber optic cables there, each one kilometer long.
The cables recorded temperature and seismic data from September 2021 to June 2024.
The data came from a one hundred meter stretch of road.
requires: Say 100 meters, never about. Do not imply the whole cable length.

claims.spoken: A team led by Penn State built a digital twin from that data.
requires: Say led by Penn State, never that Xiao is lead author.

claims.spoken: U A F's Dmitry Nicolsky is a co-author.
The model puts a neural network inside a physics solver.
The physics solver is a heat transfer model.
The network estimates the soil's unfrozen water content and thermal conductivity.
requires: Say estimates or infers. Never say these can't be measured.

claims.spoken: Those soil properties are uncertain, so the model can update them.
requires: Attribute the sentence to the Eos editor's highlight.

claims.spoken: Penn State's Ming Xiao writes that as new data arrives, the twin adjusts.
requires: Xiao wrote this in a published essay. Attribute as written, not as an interview quote.

claims.spoken: The team checked it against separate seismic data, borehole temperatures and lab measurements.
Penn State says predictions matched later field measurements more closely as the twin updated.
claims.on_screen: MATCHED LATER FIELD DATA MORE CLOSELY
requires: Paraphrase of Penn State. State no number.

claims.spoken: The paper was published in the Journal of Geophysical Research, Earth Surface, in 2026.
The work was supported by the U.S. National Science Foundation.
Xiao's essay says Arctic temperatures are rising two to three times faster than the global average.
In Utqiagvik, a bluff partly collapsed in twenty twenty three and twenty twenty four.
requires: Say the eroding edge came close to roads and buildings.

claims.spoken: A separate study by Xiao's team looked at the whole Arctic Coastal Plain.
requires: Not the digital twin. Keep the two apart.

claims.spoken: Under high emissions, it projects less than ten percent of infrastructure at risk by mid century.
requires: Scenario: high emissions. Projection from the separate study.

claims.spoken: By the twenty ninetys, about eighty percent of buildings, sixty percent of roads and ninety percent of pipelines.
requires: Under high emissions only. Projection from the separate study, ranges 80 to 83, 58 to 60, 87 to 90.

claims.spoken: A 2025 study put permafrost thaw losses to Alaska buildings and roads at thirty seven to fifty one billion dollars.
requires: Low end medium emissions, high end high emissions. Period 2015-2024 to 2055-2064. Not by 2100, not per year.

claims.spoken: The twin was tested on one road in one town.
requires: No other site appears in the sources.

claims.spoken: It predicts ground temperature and soil properties, not when a road will fail.
It is a research framework the team plans to keep refining, not a system anyone has deployed.
requires: Nothing says it is deployed. Say the sources report no deployment.

claims.spoken: Xiao said ten more years of data would be extremely valuable.
requires: Quote: If we have, say, 10 more years of data, that would be extremely valuable.

claims.spoken: The public summaries report no accuracy number for the model.
claims.on_screen: NO ACCURACY NUMBER IN PUBLIC SUMMARIES
requires: The paper itself is paywalled and unread. Say public summaries, never the paper.

claims.spoken: The sources say this is the team's first attempt to apply a digital twin to their earlier monitoring work.
claims.on_screen: FIRST DIGITAL-TWIN ATTEMPT FOR THEIR MONITORING WORK
requires: Not the first permafrost twin anywhere.
